why:
D11. A Gradle build states the architecture of an Android app, and nothing else in the repository does: `settings.gradle.kts` declares what the modules *are*, and each script declares what its module depends on. Read as Kotlin source these files would instead yield a phantom component per module and a phantom function per DSL block, which is why `.kts` has a dedicated reader rather than riding the Kotlin front-end.

Modules keep their own `gradle:` prefix and the id **is** the directory path, because a Gradle module is a directory and not a namespace — it has no package, and several modules routinely publish into the same one. That is also what lets a source file be attributed to its module by path alone, with no ownership edge invented.

The refusals are the point of the case. `libs.kotlinx.datetime` is a version-catalog coordinate for a third-party artifact: no node, no edge. `project(shared)` passes a variable, so the dependency exists but its target is not knowable from this file — it yields nothing rather than a guess resolved from the `val` above it. `testImplementation` **does** produce an edge, because a test dependency is a real dependency that a change to `core:model` can break.
excluded: `implementation(libs.kotlinx.datetime)` and `implementation(libs.androidx.core.ktx)` are third-party version-catalog coordinates. They are deliberately not nodes and not edges — a Gradle module graph is about first-party modules, and an artifact coordinate is a dependency of a different kind.

`implementation(project(shared))` names a variable. The dependency is real but its target cannot be read from this file, so nothing is emitted; resolving the `val` above it would be inference, and the same expression could be built anywhere.
The root project (`gradle:<root>`) has no build script of its own in this fixture, so it is not declared and is not labelled.

`testImplementation(project(":core:model"))` is the same edge as the `implementation` above it — edges de-duplicate by (src, dst, kind, provenance) and these differ only by line, so the relation is labelled once. §3.5 proposed tagging test configurations in provenance so `state` could separate them; `Provenance` has no field for that, so the distinction is not representable today and is recorded in the roadmap rather than faked.
